_scope: Every Statistics Canada product named by SOR/2007-303 that has no node to point at. One lead per missing publication, with the provisions that name it and a verbatim quote. Creates no edges of its own — the cluster was blocked on node coverage, not on evidence. Companion to equalization-payroll-base.json, which took the two edges whose targets already exist. UPDATE 2026-08-08: eight of the nine no-node-yet leads recorded here were closed on 2026-08-07 by src/data/research/grok-h1-equalization-named-products.json, a companion file this file's own _dropped block was never updated to reflect — the leads sat here reading as open for a day after the edges existed. See the consolidated note in _dropped below.

dependencies.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 3.1 (DIVISION 1 definitions) names the framework three times, once for each of three capital-formation aggregates: 'gross fixed capital formation in intellectual property products, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in machinery and equipment, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in non-residential structures, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. Minted 2026-08-08 (Thomas, Q1, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx): the framework is a node in its own right, matching the statute's own wording verbatim rather than an inferred release.

SOR/2007-303 s. 5(b)(i), the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base: 'the portion of the aggregate of corporate profits in Canada, before the payment of income taxes and without any deduction of the aggregate of corporate losses in Canada, that is attributable to any of the 10 provinces for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. A fourth, independent citation of the framework, distinct from the three capital-formation terms in s. 3.1. Minted 2026-08-08, same ruling.

_dropped.edge: fiscal-equalization-program -> (System of Macroeconomic Accounts, as a framework)
_dropped.why:
RESOLVED 2026-08-08 (Thomas, Q1, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx): 'these situations call for a node... it's sole role is broadcasting and that needs represented... doesn't need cadence.' Minted as statcan-system-macroeconomic-accounts in statcan-macro-accounts.json (evergreen, no releases_per_year). Two edges built here covering all four citations in this entry's own quotes (the three s. 3.1 capital-formation terms collapsed into one edge, since they cite the framework identically; the s. 5(b)(i) corporate-profits term as a second, independent edge) -- not four separate edges, since the first three are the same statutory sentence repeated for three aggregates rather than three distinct dependencies. The general question this entry raised -- 'whether a node may be a named series or framework rather than a release' -- is answered for this framework specifically; the sibling statcan-hfce / statcan-national-accounts duplication and the bea-gdp -> bea-pce question are NOT resolved by this ruling and remain open on their own terms. Original entry follows.

The most frequently named product in the Regulations and the one this graph is least able to represent. Named in the DIVISION 1 definitions at s. 3.1 three times over, for the three capital-formation aggregates: 'gross fixed capital formation in intellectual property products, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in machinery and equipment, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in non-residential structures, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. And in the DIVISION 1 revenue base at s. 5(b)(i): 'the portion of the aggregate of corporate profits in Canada, before the payment of income taxes and without any deduction of the aggregate of corporate losses in Canada, that is attributable to any of the 10 provinces for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. The CSMA is an accounting framework, not a release with a cadence, so it cannot become a node under the current model — but four separate revenue-base components depend on it definitionally, so leaving it unrepresented understates the Equalization Program's real input set. This is the same problem as the statcan-hfce / statcan-national-accounts duplication and the same problem as bea-gdp -> bea-pce, arriving from a third direction. THREE THINGS ARE NOW BLOCKED ON ONE DECISION: whether a node may be a named series or framework rather than a release.

SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(z.1): 'in the case of race track taxes described in paragraph 7(1)(z.1), the gross amount wagered in the province in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year at pari-mutuel tracks on harness and running horse races, as determined by the Canadian Pari-Mutuel Agency'. Agency named, no publication named, and no recurring titled release identified. Filed as unpublishable rather than as a lead so that a later pass does not treat it as researchable — if a CPMA publication does turn out to exist this can be reclassified, but on the regulation's wording alone there is nothing to point at.

_dropped.edge: SOR/2007-303 — table-number vintages disagree between divisions
_dropped.why: A corpus fact that will matter when these nodes are built. The same instrument cites Statistics Canada tables under two incompatible numbering systems, split by division. The Nova Scotia division uses retired CANSIM numbers: s. 8(1)(j) cites 'CANSIM table 183-0024, Sales of alcoholic beverages by volume, value and per capita 15 years and over, fiscal years ended March 31' for spirits, wine and beer in three separate subparagraphs; s. 8(1)(z) cites 'CANSIM table 002-0020'; s. 8(1)(h) and (i) cite 'CANSIM table 405-0004'. The Territorial Formula Financing part uses the current numbering for the same subject matter: s. 19(1)(f) cites 'table 10-10-0011-01, Value of sales of alcoholic beverages of liquor authorities and other retail outlets, by beverage type (× 1,000)' for the same three beverages. And the general Interpretation at s. 1(1) uses the current numbering too, at 'table 23-10-0066-01'. CANSIM was retired in favour of the current product-identifier scheme around 2018, so DIVISION 2 is citing tables under numbers Statistics Canada no longer publishes under. Two consequences. Any node built from a CANSIM citation has to be matched to its modern successor by hand, and that match is a judgement, not a quotation. And it corroborates the scope caveat on the SEPH edge: DIVISION 2 was not revised when the rest of the instrument was, which is consistent with its role as a legacy calculation for the Nova Scotia accords rather than a live all-provinces formula.

_dropped.edge: SOR/2007-303 — which division each citation lives in
_dropped.why: Recorded because a section number alone hides it, and it determines how much any of this is worth. Of the twenty-four provisions returned in this round, twelve sit in s. 8 — DIVISION 2 — Nova Scotia, which defines revenue base 'For the purpose of sections 3.71 to 3.9 of the Act', the Nova Scotia additional-equalization provisions, and retains the pre-2007 thirty-three-source revenue structure with paragraphs running (a) to (z.5). Ten sit in s. 3.1 and s. 5, which are DIVISION 1 — Fiscal Equalization to the Provinces, the live all-provinces formula with five revenue sources. Two sit in the general Interpretation at s. 1(1). THE DIVISION 1 CITATIONS ARE THE VALUABLE ONES and they are the minority. The s. 3.1 definitions in particular are what makes Tier 2's thesis true as originally stated — every province's revenue base runs through the same handful of named products — because they are definitions and not per-province measurements. The s. 8 citations are real, verified and narrower than they look. Also worth noting on packaging: the s. 3.1 definitions carry no paragraph numbers of their own, being definitions in an interpretation section, so they are citable only as 's. 3.1, definition of X'. That is the correct answer for them and is what NO CITABLE LOCATION was meant to elicit.
